meaning: A short code sent to you for one sign-in only. It stops working after a few minutes, so an old one is useless.
clues: It helps prove that you are the person signing in.
You do not have to remember it ahead of time.
It arrives by text message or from an app, just when you need it.
It stops working after a short time, and it can be used only once.
It has three words. They start with O, T, and C.
assumes: A PIN is a number you pick and remember
A security question has an answer you set up ahead of time

decoys.meaning: A personal question you pick when you set up an account, like your first pet's name. You answer it later to prove who you are.
A way to open a phone by looking at it. The phone checks that your face matches the one it saved.
A secret number, often four digits, that you type to prove it is you, such as to unlock a phone.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, a secret handshake got you into the clubhouse. A code that works once is a handshake that changes every time!

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Never read your code to anyone who calls or texts you. A real company will not ask for it.
